items.item: The first predict (step 3) is red-teamed against the plausible wrong answer that owning your own data automatically makes it trustworthy to its consumers; the reveal at steps 4-5 corrects this by quoting the data-as-a-product standard as a separate, explicit checklist that ownership alone doesn't satisfy

at.step: Predict: does owning your own data make it trustworthy to everyone else who needs it?

items.item: The second predict (step 6) is red-teamed against the plausible wrong answer that domain ownership costs nothing extra since each domain already runs its own operational systems; the reveal at step 7 quotes Dehghani's own naming of the duplicated specialized-effort cost, directly refuting the no-extra-cost guess

at.step: Predict: does handing every domain full data ownership cost nothing extra?

items.item: The third predict (step 9) is red-teamed against the plausible wrong answer that the organizational principles (ownership, data as a product) are what matter and the platform is just convenience tooling; the reveal at step 10 quotes Dehghani's own stated reason for the self-serve platform principle, which exists specifically to absorb the cost the prior two principles would otherwise push onto every domain separately

at.step: Predict: without a shared self-serve platform yet, does the mesh still work?

items.item: Step 7's cost reveal and step 10's platform-justification reveal deliberately quote the same underlying claim (duplicated specialized infrastructure effort) from two different angles — step 7 as the cost domain ownership creates, step 10 as the reason the platform principle exists to remove it — because CHAPTER.md's own scope line treats the organizational precondition and the platform's own justification as the same mechanism, not two separate facts
